free_tier.stated: the Community Edition is free and self-hosted; Pro is a paid licence

per_object_cap.stated: no cap of its own; the cap is the storage policy's

retention.stated: as long as the operator keeps it running

egress.terms: direct client-side upload and download, so the server does not relay the bytes; the egress is the storage provider's

tooling: a Go binary with a Vue front end; REST v4 under /api/v4/*, WebDAV, and S3-compatible policy backends; the nfd-parser project ships a ce driver for it
chaining: the alternative bridge, and the better one when the upstream is an object store rather than a consumer pan, because it uploads client-side and does not relay through the VPS

limits.value: the storage policy decides; the public demo has no filesystem at all

identity_cost.detail: the operator installs it; a reader needs no account on the bridge

reliability_note: The public demo at demo.cloudreve.org answers /api/v4/site/ping with code 0 and data 4.19.1-pro and has no filesystem, so a scan that stopped at the ping would record a live instance and find nothing behind it.

evidence.proved: Community Edition is open source and Pro is a paid upgrade; features include WebDAV access, multi-cloud storage with client-side transfer, and slave storage nodes

Cloudreve describes itself as a cloud drive rather than a manager for other cloud drives, and lists 'I want to redistribute other cloud storage services to my users' as a scenario it is not suitable for
HTTP 200 with {"code":0,"data":"4.19.1-pro"}, which identifies Cloudreve v4 and its Pro build, with no anonymous filesystem

notes: A v4 instance answers /api/v4/site/ping; v3 answered a different path, and neither exposes an anonymous mount list the way AList does. That is why 1 of 169 hosts classified as Cloudreve and why the class is not a public-instance population at all.
binding_note: Its own documentation says it is not for redistributing other cloud drives, which is exactly the use this topic wants, so the constraint is architectural rather than numeric.
